Yuriev Polsky's stone church required stone, craftsmen and patrons, with carving and worship giving it religious and local importance. Maintenance, clergy and workers required supplies while neighboring households still tended fields and domestic work. Passing troops sought prayer, food or space for wounded people, limited by hosts' means. Armed visitors consumed food and lodging, while patients needed carers.
